claim: For a bounded convex planar domain \(\Omega\), let \(v_\mu\) solve \(\Delta v_\mu-\mu^2v_\mu=0\) in \(\Omega\) with \(v_\mu=1\) on \(\partial\Omega\). Fix \(\mu>0\) and an interior point \(x\), and put \(d=\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)\). Among all such pairs with the same \(\mu\) and \(d\), the exact distance-only extremal values are \(\inf v_\mu(x)=e^{-\mu d}\) and \(\sup v_\mu(x)=I_0(\mu d)^{-1}\), where \(I_0\) is the modified Bessel function. The supremum is attained exactly by the disk \(B_d(x)\); the infimum is not attained by any bounded convex domain, but tangent disks of radii tending to infinity converge to it.
integrity: The proof is analytic and exact, using the maximum principle, supporting-line geometry, the radial Bessel solution on a disk, and the standard leading asymptotic of the modified Bessel function. No numerical experiment or external certification is used.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is planar and restricted to bounded convex domains. It does not claim the corresponding higher-dimensional optimal radial profile or any nonconvex analogue; an equivalent elementary comparison theorem may exist in older potential-theory terminology.
title: Sharp distance-only envelopes for the planar modified Helmholtz Dirichlet profile
